_about: Machine-readable mirror of analysis/index_drift_cause_analysis.md (PR Y).  Per-bucket cause hypotheses + confidence + next action; no bucket is labelled a confirmed CBDB bug.  See the .md for prose.

buckets.likely_cause: PHP wrote a sentinel / overflow value (>= 9999); Access wrote a real computed year.
buckets.supporting_algorithm_evidence: Per PR N runtime Access has no matching sentinel branch.
buckets.supporting_row_evidence: K1 bucket holds 1 row with php_index_year carrying the sentinel.
buckets.next_action: Forward upstream as candidate sentinel-write bug in cbdb-online-main-server PHP rebuild.  Out of scope for this repo.

buckets.confidence: tcode='05' × 7: supported_by_focused_probe (PR Z).  tcode='11' × 5: medium.  Phase-C tcodes (14/20/2304): medium.  tcode='07' × 1: medium (vestigial-vs-intentional unresolved).

buckets.likely_cause: Upstream source-data drift between User MDB and SQLite snapshot for the EVIDENCE persons that the rule reads from — NOT algorithm divergence.  Per PR AI's per-row probe (-20 sub-cluster, 9 rows): 7/9 are BIOG_MAIN.c_birthyear differing by exactly the index_year diff for the same evidence person; 2/9 are KIN_DATA evidence-pid set differing.  Per PR AJ (+1 sub-cluster, 5 rows): 4/5 are KIN_DATA evidence-pid drift, 1/5 is BIOG_MAIN birthyear drift.  All 14 / 14 rows are PHP-side / SQLite-snapshot upstream data drift; same general class as PR Z's tcode='05' candidate_php_entry_code_mapping_gap.  The Access vs PHP rule body is identical and runs correctly on both sides.
buckets.supporting_algorithm_evidence: PR N pairs each of rules 11/13/15/19 as matched (or matched_minor_diff on staging-vs-subquery aggregate).  PR AI (analysis/probe_index_year_diff_minus_20_cluster.py) and PR AJ (analysis/probe_index_year_diff_plus_1_cluster.py) walked all 14 rows individually and confirmed the upstream-data-drift mechanism.
buckets.supporting_row_evidence: Concrete example (PR AI): c_personid=228114 (王淑抃), father=王圖 (123710); User MDB BIOG_MAIN.c_birthyear(123710)=1557, SQLite=1577; Access fires 1557+30=1587, PHP fires 1577+30=1607, diff=-20 explained 100% by upstream birthyear drift.  Per-personid breakdown in reports/index_year_diff_minus_20_cluster_probe.json + reports/index_year_diff_plus_1_cluster_probe.json.
buckets.next_action: PHP-side / SQLite-snapshot data quality issue, not a CBDB User MDB algorithm bug.  Forward findings to cbdb-online-main-server / SQLite-snapshot-build team as upstream data-drift candidates.  Out-of-scope for this repo.

c_index_addr_id.rank_table_status: BIOG_ADDR_CODES is identical between User MDB and SQLite for all 22 addr_types (verified by PR L) — none of these buckets are explained by rank-table mismatch.

buckets.likely_cause: User MDB shipped with a c_index_addr_id that was never re-run after BIOG_ADDR_DATA was updated.  PHP re-runs weekly; the User MDB release process apparently doesn't re-run frmBaseMaintenance.CmdIndexAddress before shipping.
buckets.supporting_algorithm_evidence: PR L's recompute (rank-priority + MAX(c_sequence)) on User-MDB-side BIOG_ADDR_DATA matches what SQLite stores for all 412 rows; User MDB stores something else.  Maintenance code that would re-run this exists in PR M's frmBaseMaintenance dump.

buckets.next_action: Add release-process step: run frmBaseMaintenance.CmdIndexYear then CmdIndexAddress against the DATA mdb before shipping a new User MDB.  candidate_release_process_step; not labelled confirmed bug because maintainer may have intentional reasons.

buckets.likely_cause: All 10 are addr_type=1.  Per PR S deep dive: 10/10 have MAX(c_sequence) ties (multiple rows of same (person, addr_type) sharing same max sequence); 10/10 have 3 distinct picks among the tied rows (User stored vs SQLite stored vs PR L recompute).  No explicit secondary tie-break; storage-engine row order picks the winner non-deterministically (MariaDB / Microsoft JET / SQLite via pyodbc all order rows differently).
buckets.supporting_algorithm_evidence: PR S byte-level deep dive (reports/index_addr_same_candidates_deep_dive.json); both sides implement the documented rule (rank-priority + MAX(c_sequence)) — neither is wrong.
buckets.supporting_row_evidence: 10/10 rows show the MAX-tie + distinct-picks pattern explicitly.
buckets.next_action: Candidate algorithm improvement: add explicit secondary tie-break (e.g. MIN(c_addr_id)) to both implementations.  Either side could implement independently to reduce divergence.  candidate_release_process_or_algorithm_improvement; not a confirmed bug.

buckets.likely_cause: Both sides store a value that doesn't match the rank+MAX(c_sequence) recompute on either side — both stale.  Whatever maintenance step produced these is older than the current BIOG_ADDR_DATA on both sides.
buckets.supporting_algorithm_evidence: PR L's recompute disagrees with both stored values for all 10 rows.
buckets.next_action: Re-run maintenance on both sides and re-classify; if these rows move into a cleaner bucket, framing is confirmed.

buckets.likely_cause: Both sides' recomputes agree, yet stored values differ — most plausibly cross-pollination from a previous data exchange (one side stores the OTHER side's recompute) or stale release on one side stored against the other side's evidence at the time.
